*For engineers who already retry and fail over between AI model regions in client code, and wonder if a gateway is worth it. No Azure experience needed.*

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### tl;dr

**A gateway did not beat a well-built client.** Nothing in the tests showed API Management (APIM) performing better. Success rates matched. APIM p95 answer time was worse, by about a quarter of a second in a clean test.

**What mattered was a sin bin.** When a region refuses a call,a circuit breaker makes it sit out for the next minute. Setups with a sin bin answered every request when one region ran short. 

**When every region is out of quota, nothing helps.** Only more quota, or waiting for theresponse's `Retry-After` header was better for success rate.  

**Regions differ in speed.** From a UK laptop, UK South answered in about 300 ms, Sweden Central in 365 and West Europe in 480, and West Europe was the least steady.

**What to build:**

1. **Add a sin bin.** In the client, a 60-second circuit breaker for a region that returns a 429.
2. **Use a priority list** with the fastest region first.

**Should you stand up APIM?** Do it for operations, not speed: one set of credentials, one place for rules and monitoring. Those benefits were not tested. Goodput did not make the case for APIM.
:::

## The problem

AI services ration tokens. Each model deployment has a quota, counted per minute. When it runs out, the service refuses the call with HTTP status 429 ("Too Many Requests").

The usual fix is to deploy the same model in several regions and fall back between them. Most teams write that logic into the client. The alternative is a **gateway**: a server between your callers and the AI models that applies rules to every call. Azure API Management (APIM) is Microsoft's gateway service.

A gateway is one more service to pay for, run and debug. Is it worth it? This article tests that.

Callers send requests to the gateway. The gateway picks a region. If that region is out of quota, it refuses with a 429. The gateway can then try another region, or take the refusing region out of rotation. A client-side setup does the same job without the middle box. The gateway holds the model credentials, so callers only need the gateway's key.

## Terms you need

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Quota** | What a model deployment can handle each minute. Exceed it and calls are refused. There are two limits: tokens per minute (TPM, where a token is a chunk of text) and requests per minute. |
| **429 and `Retry-After`** | A 429 means "out of quota, try later". The reply often carries a `Retry-After` header: how many seconds to wait. A 5xx error means the service itself failed. |
| **Pool, weights, priority** | The pool is the three regions behind one name. Weights set each region's share: 90/5/5 sends 90% to UK South. Priority ranks the regions: a lower-ranked region gets traffic only when the higher ones are out. |
| **Retry** | Try a failed call again. The client can do it, or the gateway can. |
| **Circuit breaker** | The **gateway's** sin bin. After a set number of failures, a region leaves the pool for 60 seconds. You choose which errors count. All callers share it. |
| **Cool-down** | The **client's** sin bin: a timer that skips a region after it refuses a call. |

## What was tested

Three Azure AI Foundry regions each got a small quota, so quota exhaustion could be reached easily: UK South, West Europe and Sweden Central. The K6 load tool sent requests through the gateway, or straight to the regions. One setting changed at a time.

There were two stages of experiments:

- **Bursts.** A quick look at what each setting does when every region runs out of quota.
- **Gateway against client.** The main test. Each gateway setup was paired with a client built to do the same job. Both got the same steady stream of requests and the same quota, in alternating five-minute runs.

Three situations were tested:

| Situation | What it models |
|---|---|
| **Every region short** | Demand beyond all your quota |
| **Main region short** | One region overloaded, the others have room |
| **Nothing wrong** | What the gateway costs when all is healthy |

A rule was fixed before the main test. The gateway counts as better if it gets more than 2 points more success, or has a p95 answer time more than 50 ms faster. In these experiments, the rule was never met.

### The ceiling

Each deployment allowed 60 requests a minute (rpm). The test calls were tiny, so rpm limited rate before the token limit did. A gateway can move requests between regions but cannot raise that ceiling.

## How results are measured

| Measure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Success rate** | Share of requests that got a valid answer |
| **Time to answer** | The median and p95 latencies in milliseconds |
| **Throughput** | Requests handled per second |
| **Goodput** | Answered requests per second (throughput × success rate) |

A gateway that refuses everything instantly has high throughput and zero goodput. Goodput is a better measure for meaningful work rate. The animation below visualises a goodput of 9 requests a second.

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  var root = document.getElementById("plinko");
  if (!root) return;
  var canvas = root.querySelector("canvas"), ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
  var W = 440, H = 340, CX = W / 2, dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;
  canvas.width = W * dpr; canvas.height = H * dpr; ctx.scale(dpr, dpr);
  var el = function (k) { return root.querySelector("[data-" + k + "]"); };
  var reduce = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
  var BLUE = [58, 134, 200], GOOD = [76, 154, 62], BAD = [188, 71, 73], FADE = 0.5, GREY = "rgba(127,127,127,.55)";
  var TOTAL = 100, REFUSED = 10, SECONDS = 10, FALL = 1.3;
  var ROWS = 7, ROW0 = 70, ROWGAP = 22, PEGGAP = 40;
  var BIN_TOP = 250, BIN_Y = H - 12, R = 4.5, STEP = 11;
  var bins = { good: { x0: 16, x1: 292 }, bad: { x0: 322, x1: 424 } };
  var balls, started, raf, startTime;

  function slot(kind, i) {
    var b = bins[kind], cols = Math.floor((b.x1 - b.x0) / STEP);
    return { x: b.x0 + R + (i % cols) * STEP, y: BIN_Y - Math.floor(i / cols) * STEP };
  }
  function plan() {
    var fates = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < TOTAL; i++) fates.push(i < REFUSED ? "bad" : "good");
    for (var j = fates.length - 1; j > 0; j--) { var k = Math.floor(Math.random() * (j + 1)); var t = fates[j]; fates[j] = fates[k]; fates[k] = t; }
    var gi = 0, bi = 0;
    balls = fates.map(function (kind, n) {
      var s = slot(kind, kind === "good" ? gi++ : bi++), pts = [{ y: 8, x: CX }];
      for (var r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        var y = ROW0 + r * ROWGAP, want = CX + (s.x - CX) * ((r + 1) / (ROWS + 1)) + (Math.random() - .5) * 60;
        var off = CX + (r % 2 ? 0 : PEGGAP / 2);
        var gx = off + Math.round((want - off) / PEGGAP) * PEGGAP;
        pts.push({ y: y, x: Math.max(20, Math.min(W - 20, gx)) });
      }
      pts.push({ y: s.y, x: s.x });
      return { kind: kind, at: n / TOTAL * SECONDS, pts: pts, slot: s, landed: false };
    });
  }
  function posAt(b, p) {
    var y0 = b.pts[0].y, y1 = b.pts[b.pts.length - 1].y, y = y0 + (y1 - y0) * p * p, pts = b.pts;
    for (var i = 1; i < pts.length; i++) {
      if (y <= pts[i].y || i === pts.length - 1) {
        var a = pts[i - 1], c = pts[i], u = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (y - a.y) / (c.y - a.y || 1)));
        u = u * u * (3 - 2 * u);
        return { x: a.x + (c.x - a.x) * u, y: y };
      }
    }
  }
  var AMBER = "#e0a800", hl = null, lastT = 0;
  var TIPS = {
    sent: ["Sent", "Requests fired off so far. Each ball is one request leaving the caller. Every ball is ringed while you point here."],
    time: ["Time", "How long the test has run, on a 10-second clock. Throughput and goodput are counts divided by this time."],
    succ: ["Success rate", "Of the requests that finished, the share that got a valid answer (HTTP 200). Green balls out of all balls in the bins: 90 of 100 here. Refusals (HTTP 429) count against it."],
    thr: ["Throughput", "Requests handled per second, answered or refused. Every ball in either bin counts, whatever its colour. A gateway that refuses everything instantly would still score high here."],
    good: ["Goodput", "Answered requests per second: only the green balls. Throughput times success rate (10 a second at 90% is 9 a second). This is the useful work."]
  };
  function ball(x, y, kind, k, alpha, halo) {
    var to = kind === "good" ? GOOD : BAD, c = BLUE.map(function (v, i) { return Math.round(v + (to[i] - v) * k); });
    ctx.globalAlpha = alpha;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, y, R, 0, 6.2832); ctx.fillStyle = "rgb(" + c.join(",") + ")"; ctx.fill();
    if (halo) { ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, y, R + 2.5, 0, 6.2832); ctx.strokeStyle = AMBER; ctx.lineWidth = 1.6; ctx.stroke(); }
    ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
  }
  function scene(t) {
    lastT = t;
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
    ctx.fillStyle = GREY;
    for (var r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
      var off = CX + (r % 2 ? PEGGAP / 2 : 0);
      for (var k = -6; k <= 6; k++) {
        var x = off + k * PEGGAP;

        ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, ROW0 + r * ROWGAP - ROWGAP / 2, 2.5, 0, 6.2832); ctx.fill();
      }
    }
    var succ = hl === "succ";
    ctx.lineWidth = succ ? 3 : 1.5;
    ctx.strokeStyle = succ ? "rgb(" + GOOD.join(",") + ")" : GREY;
    ctx.strokeRect(bins.good.x0 - 4, BIN_TOP, bins.good.x1 - bins.good.x0 + 8, H - BIN_TOP - 2);
    ctx.strokeStyle = succ ? "rgb(" + BAD.join(",") + ")" : GREY;
    ctx.strokeRect(bins.bad.x0 - 4, BIN_TOP, bins.bad.x1 - bins.bad.x0 + 8, H - BIN_TOP - 2);
    ctx.fillStyle = GREY; ctx.font = "13px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText("Answered", bins.good.x0, BIN_TOP + 16);
    ctx.fillText("Refused", bins.bad.x0, BIN_TOP + 16);
    ctx.font = "11px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText("HTTP 200", bins.good.x0, BIN_TOP + 30);
    ctx.fillText("HTTP 429", bins.bad.x0, BIN_TOP + 30);
    var sent = 0, good = 0, landed = 0, landedGood = 0, clock = Math.min(t, SECONDS);
    balls.forEach(function (b) {
      var p = (t - b.at) / FALL;
      if (p < 0) return;
      sent++; if (b.kind === "good") good++;
      var done = p >= 1, isGood = b.kind === "good", alpha = 1, halo = false;
      if (done) { landed++; if (isGood) landedGood++; }
      if (hl === "sent") halo = true;
      else if (hl === "thr" || hl === "succ") { halo = done; alpha = done ? 1 : .35; }
      else if (hl === "good") { halo = done && isGood; alpha = halo ? 1 : .25; }
      if (done) ball(b.slot.x, b.slot.y, b.kind, Math.min(1, (p - 1) * FALL / FADE), alpha, halo);
      else { var q = posAt(b, p); ball(q.x, q.y, b.kind, 0, alpha, halo); }
    });
    if (succ) {
      ctx.font = "bold 20px sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign = "right";
      ctx.fillStyle = "rgb(" + GOOD.join(",") + ")"; ctx.fillText(landedGood, bins.good.x1, BIN_TOP + 24);
      ctx.fillStyle = "rgb(" + BAD.join(",") + ")"; ctx.fillText(landed - landedGood, bins.bad.x1, BIN_TOP + 24);
      ctx.textAlign = "left";
    }
    if (hl === "time") {
      ctx.lineWidth = 4; ctx.lineCap = "round";
      ctx.strokeStyle = GREY; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(12, 6); ctx.lineTo(W - 12, 6); ctx.stroke();
      ctx.strokeStyle = AMBER; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(12, 6); ctx.lineTo(12 + (W - 24) * clock / SECONDS, 6); ctx.stroke();
      ctx.lineCap = "butt"; ctx.fillStyle = GREY; ctx.font = "11px sans-serif";
      ctx.fillText("0 s", 12, 22); ctx.textAlign = "right"; ctx.fillText("10 s", W - 12, 22); ctx.textAlign = "left";
    }
    el("sent").textContent = sent;
    el("time").textContent = (clock >= SECONDS ? SECONDS : clock.toFixed(1)) + " s";
    if (sent > 0 && clock > 0.3) {
      el("succ").textContent = Math.round(good / sent * 100) + "%";
      el("thr").textContent = (sent / Math.max(clock, 1)).toFixed(1) + "/s";
      el("good").textContent = (good / Math.max(clock, 1)).toFixed(1) + "/s";
    }
    if (clock >= SECONDS && sent === TOTAL) {
      el("succ").textContent = "90%"; el("thr").textContent = "10/s"; el("good").textContent = "9/s";
    }
  }
  function run() {
    cancelAnimationFrame(raf); plan();
    if (reduce) { scene(SECONDS + FALL + FADE); return; }
    startTime = performance.now();
    (function frame(now) {
      var t = (now - startTime) / 1000; scene(t);
      if (t < SECONDS + FALL + FADE + .1) raf = requestAnimationFrame(frame);
    })(startTime);
  }
  var tip = document.getElementById("plinko-tip"), cards = root.querySelectorAll("[data-tip]");
  function show(card) {
    var key = card.getAttribute("data-tip");
    hl = key; Array.prototype.forEach.call(cards, function (c) { c.classList.toggle("on", c === card); });
    tip.innerHTML = "<strong>" + TIPS[key][0] + "</strong>" + TIPS[key][1];
    var rr = root.getBoundingClientRect(), cr = card.getBoundingClientRect(), sr = card.parentNode.getBoundingClientRect();
    var tw = tip.offsetWidth, mid = cr.left + cr.width / 2 - rr.left, left = Math.max(0, Math.min(rr.width - tw, mid - tw / 2));
    tip.style.left = left + "px"; tip.style.top = (sr.bottom - rr.top + 10) + "px"; tip.style.setProperty("--ax", (mid - left) + "px");
    tip.classList.add("on"); scene(lastT);
  }
  function hide() {
    hl = null; tip.classList.remove("on");
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(cards, function (c) { c.classList.remove("on"); }); scene(lastT);
  }
  Array.prototype.forEach.call(cards, function (c) {
    c.addEventListener("mouseenter", function () { show(c); });
    c.addEventListener("focus", function () { show(c); });
    c.addEventListener("click", function () { show(c); });
    c.addEventListener("mouseleave", hide);
    c.addEventListener("blur", hide);
  });
  root.querySelector(".plinko-replay").addEventListener("click", run);
  plan(); scene(0);
  if ("IntersectionObserver" in window) {
    var io = new IntersectionObserver(function (e) {
      if (!started && e.some(function (x) { return x.isIntersecting; })) { started = true; io.disconnect(); run(); }
    }, { threshold: 0.5 });
    io.observe(root);
  } else { run(); }
})();
</script>
```


## What happened

### 1. Every region short

Nothing helped. In 200-request bursts, nearly every setup answered about 17%. A circuit breaker on an even split made it worse (4.5%). Only a client that waited as long as `Retry-After` asked got nearly everything through (99.5%). That took about 30 seconds per request.

```{=html}
<iframe
  class="shaded_box"
  title="Interactive scatter of the APIM burst experiments"
  src="/./www/24-apim-load-balance-perf/scatter.html"
  loading="lazy"
  referrerpolicy="no-referrer"
  style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:960px;height:720px;margin:0 auto;border:none;overflow:hidden;">
</iframe>
<p class="rp-fig" style="text-align:center;margin-top:.35rem;color:#52606d;">goodput = throughput × success rate</p>
```

### 2. Main region short

Here the setup mattered. UK South got 90% of the traffic, more than it could serve. The other two regions sat nearly idle.

| Setup | Success |
|---|---:|
| Nothing | 70% |
| Retry only, in the gateway | 77% |
| Retry only, in the client | 79% |
| **Sin bin in the gateway** (circuit breaker or priority list) | **100%** |
| **Sin bin in the client** (cool-down) | **100%** |
| Client tries UK South first, nothing remembered | 100% |

- **Retry alone barely helped.** Each retry picked a region again by weight, so nine in ten went straight back to the region that had just said no.
- **A sin bin fixed it.** The region sat out, and every call went where there was room.
- **Trip on the first failure.** It was safe at every rate tested, and it wasted the fewest calls.
- **No sin bin costs calls.** Trying UK South first took 1.4 calls per request. A sin bin took about 1.1.
- **The gateway matched the client.** Same success. The p95 was 880-1,040 ms through the gateway and 640-770 ms through the client.

Raising the load did not change this.

### 3. Nothing wrong

Both sides answered everything. The median answer took 372 ms through the gateway and 396 ms direct. The p95 was 710 ms against 593 ms. The gateway's cost is in the slow tail. The next section looks at that more closely.

### 4. How fast is each region?

A separate set of tests measured speed alone. Quota was plentiful, each request got one attempt, and there was no retry, no sin bin and no cool-down. Calls went straight to each region, then through the gateway pinned to one region at a time.

| Region | Direct: median | Direct: p95 | Via gateway: median | Via gateway: p95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UK South | 297 ms | 434 ms | 299 ms | 798 ms |
| Sweden Central | 365 ms | 675 ms | 396 ms | 929 ms |
| West Europe | 481 ms | 982 ms | 473 ms | 1,233 ms |

- **The order held.** UK South was fastest, Sweden Central about 65 ms behind, West Europe slowest. The same order appeared in all three repeats across the day, and in a one-region-at-a-time check.
- **West Europe was the least steady.** Its median ranged from 450 to 764 ms between runs. The others moved by about 10 ms.
- **The gateway added nothing visible to the median** for UK South and West Europe, and about 30 ms for Sweden Central.
- **It did raise the p95.** By 250-360 ms in every region. This time there was no retry, no breaker and no quota pressure, so those are not the cause. The extra hop is still the best guess. It is a guess.

All of this was measured from one laptop in the UK on one day. A caller elsewhere could see a different order.

## What to build

1. **Add a sin bin.** Whether in the client or the gateway, this is the one thing that made a difference. Retrying without it mostly sends calls back to the region that just refused.
2. **In a gateway, use a priority list for one main region and some fallbacks.** Rank them by speed from where your callers are. From the UK that meant UK South, then Sweden Central, then West Europe. Add a circuit breaker that counts 429s and trips on the first failure. A breaker that counts only 5xx never fires on quota errors.
3. **Handle the 503.** If every region is short, a breaker on 429 can empty the pool. Callers then get instant 503s.
4. **Mind the retry pause.** In one test, a one-second pause pushed the p95 to 2.6 seconds. With no pause it was about 1 second (two runs).
5. **Use `Retry-After` for batch work only.** Waiting out the minute suits a nightly job. It does not suit a chat.
6. **Do not cap requests below real demand.** The cap will refuse work that would have succeeded.
7. **Buy quota before you tune routing.** When every region is short, nothing else helps.

## Should you stand up APIM? {#should-you-stand-up-apim}

**What it will not do.** Create quota. Beat a good client on success or speed. Fix retries on its own.

**What it can give you.** These are the usual reasons. None were tested.

- One place for credentials. Callers hold one gateway key, not a key per region.
- One place to change routing. No client redeploys.
- One place to log, cap and watch every call.
- The same behaviour for every team and language.

**What it costs.** Another service to run and pay for. The p95 was 250-360 ms higher. New ways to fail (see Before you go live). A shared dependency for every caller.

**How to decide.**

- **A few callers, one team, one language:** add the sin bin to the client. Skip the gateway.
- **Many callers or teams, credentials you would rather not spread, or routing you must change fast:** a gateway is worth considering. Buy it for those reasons, not for speed.

## Before you go live

Checks for anyone running this in production.

| What goes wrong | What to do |
|---|---|
| **APIM retry silently does nothing on requests with a body.** The retry fails inside the gateway and never reaches the model. | Add `buffer-request-body="true"` to the forward-request inside the retry. Then confirm the model sees more than one call per refused request. |
| **A retry block with no forward-request returns instant fake 200s.** | Alert on answers that come back far faster than the model can respond (here, 14 ms against hundreds). Check the body holds a real answer. |
| **`count` means retries, not attempts.** `count="3"` is four attempts. | Match your client's attempts to the gateway's. |
| **Policy changes take up to two minutes. Breaker state survives a redeploy.** | Wait two minutes after a change before you trust it. |
| **The request limit can bite before the token limit.** Here it was 60 requests a minute alongside 60,000 tokens. | Read your limits first: `az cognitiveservices account deployment show`, then `properties.rateLimits`. |
| **Turning a breaker off with an empty rules list is rejected.** | Set the breaker to `null` in Terraform or ARM. |

## Limits

- **Tiny calls.** Real prompts hit the token limit first.
- **Developer tier.** One gateway unit, no SLA. Production tiers will differ. On multi-unit tiers each instance keeps its own [breaker state](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/backends).
- **Gateway and client were not identical.** The gateway paused one second between retries and the client none. The gateway shared its sin bin across all callers. The client kept one per simulated caller. The client ran from a laptop. The gateway sat in UK South.
- **Few runs for some setups.** Ten runs were discarded when the laptop slept. Several setups have two or three valid runs. The cards list every one.
- **The slow tail is unexplained.** The speed tests ruled out retry, breakers and quota. The extra hop is the best guess. It is a guess.
- **Region speed came from one laptop in the UK, over one day.** West Europe moved a lot between runs. The one-region-at-a-time check has one run per region. For West Europe the gateway's slow-tail cost overlaps with the spread between direct runs, so it is less clear there than in UK South and Sweden Central.
- **The bursts ran with a broken retry rule.** They show what weights and breakers do, not what a working retry does in a burst. The steady runs had working retry.
- **The measured ceiling sat about 20% above the configured limit.** The reason is unknown.
- **Success means a valid answer.** Answer quality was not judged.

## What to test next {#what-to-test-next}

- **The slow tail.** The speed tests already compared a bare gateway with direct calls. What is left is the cause. APIM's diagnostic logs split each request into total time and time waiting on the model. Then run the client from a machine in UK South, and repeat on a production tier.
- **Region speed from elsewhere.** Repeat the speed tests from a machine in each region, and over several days.
- **Real prompts.** Longer prompts would hit the token limit first.
- **One shared client.** A single cool-down shared by all callers, as most services run.
- **The operational case.** Count what a gateway saves: credential rotation, a routing change across several codebases.


## Appendix: all the runs {#all-the-runs}

Every success-rate run, as a card. The speed tests follow the cards as a table. Each tab holds runs that share a quota and load, so compare cards within a tab. The first four tabs are the gateway-against-client tests: a coloured edge is the gateway and a grey edge is a client calling the regions directly. The last five are the 200-request bursts. A reference card is pinned on most tabs. Hover a numbered note to highlight that part of the card.

### Test setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Gateway | APIM Developer tier, UK South |
| Regions | Azure AI Foundry in UK South, West Europe and Sweden Central |
| Model | `gpt-4.1-mini`, answers of about 5 tokens, one fixed prompt |
| Quota | 10,000 TPM per region for the bursts, 60,000 TPM for everything else |
| Load tool | [Grafana k6](https://k6.io) on a Mac laptop |
| Bursts | 200 requests from 20 simulated callers, sent as fast as possible |
| Steady runs | 1, 2, 3 or 6 requests a second for five minutes |
| Gaps | 60 seconds between runs, 2 minutes after a policy change |
| Success | HTTP 200 with a valid answer in the body |
| Discarded | Steady runs longer than 330 seconds (the laptop slept) or with dropped requests |
| Speed tests | Rebuilt regions and gateway, 60,000 TPM per region, one request every 2 seconds per region for about 11 minutes, first 20 per region ignored |

The Terraform, k6 scripts and results are in <a href="https://github.com/r-leyshon/azure-load-balance-perf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">r-leyshon/azure-load-balance-perf</a>.

### Region speed runs

Median and p95 answer times, in milliseconds. About 300 answers per region per run. Every valid run had zero refusals and zero errors. Ranges are across runs.

| Test | Region | Runs | Median | p95 |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Direct, regions mixed in one run | UK South | 3 | 297 (296-306) | 434 (428-442) |
| Direct, regions mixed in one run | Sweden Central | 3 | 365 (361-372) | 675 (656-749) |
| Direct, regions mixed in one run | West Europe | 3 | 481 (450-764) | 982 (816-1,212) |
| Direct, one region per run | UK South | 1 | 284 | 385 |
| Direct, one region per run | Sweden Central | 1 | 364 | 749 |
| Direct, one region per run | West Europe | 1 | 575 | 1,000 |
| Gateway pinned to one region | UK South | 3 | 299 (297-310) | 798 (729-874) |
| Gateway pinned to one region | Sweden Central | 3 | 396 (383-402) | 929 (806-973) |
| Gateway pinned to one region | West Europe | 3 | 473 (459-517) | 1,233 (1,063-1,286) |

Two mixed-region runs were discarded and repeated because each dropped one request. The repeats were valid. For the gateway runs, Azure Monitor confirmed that every call reached only the pinned region. The rules for judging a difference were written down before the first run. The gateway's pinned set-up had no breaker and no retry, and the normal settings were restored and read back afterwards.

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  var reduce = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
  function parseValue(text) {
    var match = String(text).trim().match(/^([\d.]+)(.*)$/);
    if (!match) return null;
    return { n: parseFloat(match[1]), suffix: match[2] || "", d: (match[1].split(".")[1] || "").length };
  }
  document.querySelectorAll(".exp-grid .exp-card").forEach(function (card) {
    var bars = [];
    card.querySelectorAll(".mbar").forEach(function (row) {
      var fill = row.querySelector(".track i");
      var label = row.querySelector(".v");
      if (!fill || !label) return;
      var pct = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(fill).getPropertyValue("--pct")) || parseFloat(fill.style.getPropertyValue("--pct")) || 0;
      var parsed = parseValue(label.textContent);
      if (!parsed) return;
      bars.push({ fill: fill, label: label, pct: pct, n: parsed.n, suffix: parsed.suffix, d: parsed.d });
      if (!reduce) {
        fill.style.setProperty("--pct", "0");
        label.textContent = (0).toFixed(parsed.d) + parsed.suffix;
      }
    });
    if (!bars.length || reduce || !("IntersectionObserver" in window)) return;
    var played = false;
    var observer = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
      if (played || !entries.some(function (e) { return e.isIntersecting; })) return;
      played = true;
      observer.disconnect();
      var start = performance.now();
      var duration = 900;
      function frame(now) {
        var t = Math.min(1, (now - start) / duration);
        var eased = 1 - Math.pow(1 - t, 3);
        bars.forEach(function (bar) {
          bar.fill.style.setProperty("--pct", String(bar.pct * eased));
          bar.label.textContent = (bar.n * eased).toFixed(bar.d) + bar.suffix;
        });
        if (t < 1) requestAnimationFrame(frame);
      }
      requestAnimationFrame(frame);
    }, { threshold: 0.35 });
    observer.observe(card);
  });
})();
</script>
```
